intro.data: Encode is reversible, and so is Compress. Chain two reversible steps and the whole journey is reversible. But one finishing machine isn't truly reversible — it loses detail. Pick the lossless one to reach the archive.
intro.alchemy: Grind is reversible, and so is Mint. Chain two reversible steps and the whole journey is reversible. One finisher loses detail — pick the lossless one to reach the coin.
intro.spellcraft: Etch is reversible, and so is Seal. Chain two reversible steps and the whole working is reversible. One finisher loses detail — pick the lossless one to reach the ward.
intro.abstract: f and the right h are isomorphisms; chained, the composite is too. Avoid the lossy look-alike.

goal.data: Chain two lossless machines to reach the archive.
goal.alchemy: Chain two lossless apparatuses to reach the coin.
goal.spellcraft: Chain two lossless runes to reach the ward.
goal.abstract: Reach C via two reversible steps.

description.data: packs the data into a blob
description.spellcraft: etches the spark into a glyph

afterSuccess.data: Two lossless steps make a lossless whole — Encode then Compress can be undone (decompress, then decode), so the start and the archive are the same up to renaming. Flatten would have lost detail and broken reversibility.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Two lossless steps make a lossless whole — the coin can be returned to the bar. Melt would have lost detail.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Two lossless steps make a lossless whole — the ward can be returned to the sigil. Smear would have lost detail.
afterSuccess.abstract: Two isomorphisms compose to an isomorphism; the lossy look-alike does not. A ≅ C.

reveal.summary: Isomorphisms compose: if A ≅ B and B ≅ C then A ≅ C, with inverse f⁻¹ ∘ h⁻¹. A lossy step breaks reversibility.
notation: A ≅ B and B ≅ C ⟹ A ≅ C
reveal.moreFormal: Isomorphism is an equivalence relation on objects; it composes and reverses. Reversibility is exactly losing no information.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: Compose two lossless codecs and you can still round-trip; one lossy step ruins it.
